name: Christ the King
kicker: Christ the King on Small Mountain
summary: A 32 m Christ on Small Mountain: climb about 800 steps in the morning for the view of the city and sea. About 100 more steps take you up to the shoulders. Entry is free; dress as for a religious site. A motorbike taxi is the other way up. The white Mary on Big Mountain is a different statue.
getThere: Steps from the end of Back Beach, or a motorbike taxi.
heroCaption: Christ the King, both arms out, on Small Mountain

notice.title: Mary is the other white statue
notice.body: Our Lady of Mulberry Beach, on Big Mountain, is also white and 32 metres tall. She holds the Child. Christ stands on Small Mountain with both arms out.

body: The statue stands on Small Mountain above the point where Back Beach meets Pineapple Beach. It dates from 1974 and is 32 metres tall. You climb about 800 steps to the feet, then about 100 more to the shoulders, where people stand on the arms to look over the city and the sea.
Go in the morning, before the heat makes the climb hard. Dress as you would for a church. Entry is free. If you would rather not climb, take a motorbike taxi.
The lighthouse is on the same headland. Make it your second stop, for the sunset over the East Sea.

figures.caption: The head, the halo, and both arms, with people standing on the arms
figures.alt: Close view of Christ the King in Vung Tau, arms outstretched

gettingThere: Small Mountain is the southern headland of the peninsula. The steps start where Back Beach meets Pineapple Beach. A motorbike taxi from either beach is the other way up.

legs.heading: From Back Beach
legs.body: Walk or ride to the south end of the beach, then climb about 800 steps to the feet.

legs.heading: From Front Beach
legs.body: Taxi or motorbike taxi round Small Mountain to the foot of the steps.

admissionNote: Free. Dress as for a religious site.
